newsitem.title: GERMANY: No differences on EU between Paris and Bonn -Chirac.
newsitem.headline: No differences on EU between Paris and Bonn -Chirac.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac insisted in a German newspaper interview published on Tuesday that there were no major differences between Paris and Bonn on European policy.

"Our vision of the world is identical, and from that comes our vision of Europe," Chirac was quoted as saying in Tuesday's Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung daily, dismissing reports of differences between him and Chancellor Helmut Kohl.

Chirac also said there was complete accord between Bonn and Paris on European monetary union (EMU) -- the timetable for its introduction would be observed and it was still necessay to make savings as neither France nor Germany had yet reached the budget deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product.
Chirac, who visited Bonn last week, admitted various external circumstances had prevented him and Kohl from getting together as often as they had planned for informal talks.
But he said they had spoken frequently by telephone and agreed to try to meet more often in the future.

He said he was sure differences over the details of reforming European Union institutions would be overcome in the next few weeks, the newspaper reported. He planned to meet Kohl in Paris next month to agree a common position.

Chirac also spoke out against any delay to the end of the intergovernmental conference (IGC) charged with formulating proposals for EU reform. The IGC is scheduled to present its conclusions to an EU summit in Amsterdam in June.
Chirac said experience showed breakthroughs were often made at the last minute and the time pressure was necessary if the EU wanted to admit new members in the year 2000.
On the subject of Franco-German cooperation, Chirac said the delay in some joint projects such as the Helios spy satellite was due to the need for consolidation in both nations' budgets.
"Every mark and every franc counts at the moment. There is no lack of ideas or lack of will, rather we lack the means just now. But that will change," he said.
